evidence: Turner explicitly gives Gujarati/Marathi rĩgṇī eggplant (Solanum jacquinii), Gujarati rĩgṇũ fruit and Marathi rĩgṇẽ under riṅgaṇī. These Bhili/Nimadi survey r(i)ŋ(g)aṇ- forms fit that western plant-name family, including weakened or unrecorded g; the generic survey eggplant sense does not identify the exact botanical species or prove Turner’s tentative deeper connection with riṅg creep.

Turner’s first vātiṅgaṇa branch explicitly includes Oriya bāiṅgaṇa, Punjabi baĩgaṇ/vaĩgaṇ and Hindi baigan/baĩgun. These intact Oriya/Gujari/Haryanvi/Pothwari responses fit that inherited regional family. The retained-t northwestern forms, explicitly traced through Iranian in Turner, and responses containing a second crop name are excluded.

Turner gives Bihari bhaṇṭā and Maithili/Awadhi bhā̃ṭā eggplant under bhaṇṭākī. Majhi bh(y)enṭā/bhyānṭā and Nimadi bhāṭṭe match that bh–ṭ plant-name family with regional vowel and stop-cluster outcomes. The i-vowel bhiṇṭikā subgroup with Nepali bhĩṛā/bhẽṛā is not selected.

Turner explicitly includes Hindi dhūl and Western Pahari/Jaunsari dhūṛ dust, with Kotgarhi dhvḷo. These Haryanvi, Jaunsari and Kullui forms preserve the dust stem with ordinary regional vowels/endings; this excludes longer dhūdhar and rajas-like responses whose extra morphology needs separate evidence.

Turner gives both Oriya dhuḷi and dialectal dhūri dust within the same dhūḍi/dhūli family. The neighbouring Bhatri/Adivasi Oriya duṛli/dūrli forms contain both liquids and are placed in that family as a qualified regional comparison, not as evidence for an asserted regular insertion rule. The source’s aspiration and liquid spellings are unchanged.
